episodes.182501: Scattered thunderstorms moved across far northern Illinois during the early morning of August 17th producing isolated large hail.
episodes.182660: Abundant subtropical moisture paired with weak steering flow resulted in slow moving showers and thunderstorms across the higher terrain of western Colorado. Some of the stronger storms produced heavy rain which led to debris flows in portions of Garfield County, including on the Grizzly Creek Fire burn scar in Glenwood Canyon. Flooding also occurred in portions of Moffat County due to heavy rain from storms.
episodes.182671: As the ridge of high pressure moved into a more favorable position near the Southern Plains, eastern Utah was able to access the deeper monsoon moisture. This led to increased coverage of showers and thunderstorms. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain which led to some flooding in portions of Grand County.
episodes.183107: Strong storms moving offshore produced wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.183305: Stong sea breeze formation and high moisture quantities led to another day of showers and thunderstorms on August 17th. The most active weather primarily focused over portions of the east coast recently impacted by high rainfall. Metro Palm Beach, Miami-Dade, and Broward counties grounds were very saturated from rainfall, so the land was prone to flooding.
episodes.183623: A cold front resulted in a broken line of thunderstorms moving into Illinois during the early morning hours of August 17. Isolated hail occurred as a result of the storms.
episodes.183639: A tropical wave with its axis between Puerto Rico and the Mona Passage produced strong thunderstorms with gusty winds and flooding rains across Puerto Rico on the 17th of August. In addition, a waterspout developed off the northwestern coast of PR.
episodes.183640: A tropical wave with its axis between Puerto Rico and the Mona Passage produced strong thunderstorms with gusty winds and flooding rains across Puerto Rico on the 17th of August. In addition, a waterspout developed off the northwestern coast of PR.
episodes.183881: Abundant monsoon moisture triggered thunderstorms with heavy rain and flash flooding over central Arizona.
episodes.183994: SW steering flow with the passing of a mid-level short wave trough triggered strong storms near the sea breeze merger toward the Atlantic coast in the afternoon over a moist and unstable airmass.
episodes.184415: A severe thunderstorm tracked through the southeast portion of the forecast area and produced 1 to 1.25 inch diameter hail and locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184505: A cold front moved southeastward across Iowa and into northwest Illinois, with a line of showers and thunderstorms developing ahead of the front. Some of these storms became severe and produced hail ranging in size from penny to golf ball size.
episodes.184511: Isolated thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees in Oro Valley. In Sierra Vista, heavy rain caused a roof to collapse in a commercial building and lightning sparked a fire at a nearby apartment complex.
episodes.184518: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced damaging winds and large hail in Marana.  A funnel cloud was also observed.
episodes.184694: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.184785: A cold front moving through an unstable air mass generated strong thunderstorms over portions of western Lake Superior during the evening of the 16th.
episodes.184786: A cold front moving through an unstable air mass generated strong thunderstorms over northern Lake Michigan on the early morning of the 17th.
episodes.184801: Extremely heavy rainfall caused some flash flooding in the Pocatello area and American Falls.   One to 2.5 inches of rain fell in a 3 hour time span.
episodes.184802: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 16th across northwest Wisconsin ahead of a cold front. Daytime heating led to strong instability over the region and a strong low level jet provided ample wind shear for storms to work with. With the cold front, the storms were generally linear in mode resulting in damaging winds being the primary threat as they moved to the east. Numerous reports of tree damage were received from across northwest Wisconsin into the evening hours along with a few hail reports. The largest hail report was half dollar-sized.
episodes.184810: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours of the 16th across northeastern Minnesota ahead of a cold front. Daytime heating led to strong instability over the region and a strong low level jet provided ample wind shear for storms to work with. The storms didn't really get organized until they moved into northwest Wisconsin, but one storm did produce nickel-sized hail in Sandstone.
episodes.185027: Monsoonal flash flooding brought a variety of impacts to southern Utah, including flash flooding in Capitol Reef National Park that prompted evacuation of a campground and road closures.
episodes.185048: A lingering cold front, weak meso low and remnant outflow boundaries along with an environment displaying deep moisture and modest instability led to strong thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds and flooding across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.185053: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced strong winds just northeast of Buffalo Gap.
episodes.185078: A lingering cold front, weak meso low and remnant outflow boundaries along with an environment displaying deep moisture and modest instability led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds across coastal waters.
episodes.185084: Isolated thunderstorms impacted the southern coastal waters of North Carolina on the morning of the 17th. These storms brought strong wind gusts to the area.
episodes.185125: An isolated line of thunderstorms moved through western Martin County on the evening of August 16th, 2023. One thunderstorm became severe and produced nickel to quarter size hail and gusty winds that nearly blew away tents at the Martin County fairgrounds in Fairmont, MN.
episodes.185450: An isolated waterspout was observed southeast of Dry Tortugas National Park.  A broad lower-tropospheric ridge was aligned west-southwest through east-northeast across the Florida Keys.
episodes.185555: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms embedded in westerly synoptic flow south of a stalled frontal boundary over the northern Gulf of Mexico produce a waterspout near Anna Maria Island as well as gusty winds across Tampa Bay and neighboring waters.
episodes.185569: Evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce funnel cloud near Lehigh Acres in Lee County.

One to two inches of rain fell in Chubbuck in a 3 hour time frame and caused some flash flooding on roads and a few basements.  The interstate 86 underpass on Hawthorne Road flooded. Garage and basement flooding in the Chubbuck and Galena Road area.

Thunderstorms winds downed power poles near Emigh and Sandario Rds. At nearby Marana High School, trees and saguaros were downed, solar paneled parking covers were heavily damaged, and one building sustained minor roof damage. At the athletic facilities, fences were damaged and the football field turf was rolled up by the wind and damaged. Classes were not held the next day due to a power outage and debris cleanup. Elsewhere, power poles were downed near Twin Peaks and Silverbell Roads and an empty tractor-trailer was overturned near Avra Valley and Sandario Roads. A wind gust to 64 mph was recorded at the KAVQ AWOS at 1535MST.
